I got it working with both `-gdwarf-4` and `-gdwarf-5` after changing the optimization level to `-O1` to have smaller debuginfo.

My build with `-O2` has debuginfo that exceeds 2 GiB, and so it gets split forcefully into a separate 2GB `.debugsymbols` file. And so libbacktrace seems to struggle either with the file being separate, or with it being over 2GB still.

Rebased to include #100281, this should now work fine regardless of the binary size.
Only tested GCC so far.

Note that we're not using libbacktrace for Linux currently, only for Windows/mingw.

We could, though, if there's benefit to it compared to our current code.

> Note that we're not using libbacktrace for Linux currently, only for Windows/mingw.

If it's working reliably (was not when I last tested, but it was a long time ago), the only benefit probably is getting rid of dependency on external `addr2line` (or `atos` on macOS, but it's less relevant, I think it's part of base system install).

`addr2line` is part of binutils which should be relatively ubiquitous on Linux setups that are suitable for gaming or gamedev. But it's true that the dependency _can_ be missing, e.g. it's not preinstalled in Fedora's minimal docker image (but that image is kept as minimal as possible by design).

I don't think it's been an issue up until now so I'd say let's not fix what isn't broken, and keep the current implementation.

> Note that we're not using libbacktrace for Linux currently, only for Windows/mingw.
